scope: All 22 maintained frontier targets in frontier_physics_target_register_v1.json.

commonProtocol.searchMode: Exact phrases, field synonyms and mechanism-plus-observable combinations; inspect the primary seed's reference list backward and search its exact title, authors and key mechanism forward.
commonProtocol.negativeSearchRule: Failure to find a paper is recorded only as a dated search result, never as proof of nonexistence.
commonProtocol.sourceRule: Technical findings are taken from primary papers or official research repositories. Reviews may supply vocabulary but cannot alone establish a frontier claim.

records.label: Open-system contractive selection
queries: open quantum systems reservoir engineering contractive dynamics process tomography
quantum reservoir process reconstruction nonideal dynamics

backwardCitationSearch.result: Reference chain confirms reservoir processing and bosonic process reconstruction as conventional mechanisms.

forwardCitationSearch.query: "Experimental demonstration of enhanced quantum tomography via quantum reservoir processing" citing related
forwardCitationSearch.result: No source found that derives the corpus selector datum from symmetry alone.

strongestSupport.finding: A physical reservoir can learn a nonideal dynamical map and improve held-out state reconstruction.

strongestOpposition.finding: Open-system predictions depend on an explicit bath model; dissipation is not supplied by kinematics.

records.presentBounds: Finite platforms support map reconstruction and engineered attraction; platform-independent selection is not established.
records.conflicts: Tomographic success can reflect learned apparatus dynamics rather than a source-derived selector.
records.negativeSearchReceipt: No primary source found deriving the independently calibrated Y datum from Spin(2,3) or Jordan closure.
records.residualNoveltyClaim: Jointly test holonomy, Y-removal, contraction, conditioned records and thermodynamic cost on one carrier.
records.updateTrigger: A physical carrier reports the full preregistered return-map and Y-off control.

strongestSupport.finding: Resolved detector records can restore rank lost by state-only summaries after response and nuisance propagation.

strongestOpposition.finding: Local Fisher rank does not by itself establish global identifiability or attainable precision.

records.presentBounds: Finite declared mechanism libraries can be separated; unrestricted mechanisms remain quotient classes.

records.negativeSearchReceipt: No primary result makes one finite detector globally injective over unrestricted physics.
records.residualNoveltyClaim: Design the cheapest added channel that splits the worst calibrated equivalence fibre.

records.label: Same-carrier thermoelectric--Casimir closure
queries: Casimir force Weyl semimetal Hall conductivity Lifshitz

backwardCitationSearch.result: The force literature requires the full optical response, geometry and magnetic orientation.

forwardCitationSearch.query: "Casimir force between Weyl semimetals in a chiral medium" experiment Hall film
forwardCitationSearch.result: Theory has advanced, but no same-specimen Hall/Nernst-to-force closure was found.

strongestSupport.finding: Hall response and orientation can materially change a Weyl-semimetal Casimir force.

strongestOpposition.finding: Thermoelectric response, especially Nernst response, remains scattering- and parameter-dependent.

records.presentBounds: Topological-material Casimir effects are theoretically allowed; broadband same-film off-diagonal response and nuisance-beating force data remain absent.
records.conflicts: Low-frequency Hall topology does not determine the full imaginary-frequency tensor.
records.negativeSearchReceipt: No primary paper was found making a no-refit Casimir prediction from the same film's Hall, Seebeck and Nernst data.
records.residualNoveltyClaim: One frozen causal tensor should predict a differential force or torque without post-force refitting.
records.updateTrigger: Release of matched-film broadband complex tensor and force covariance.
